description: Phase 6bv gate — SQLite-compat quirk: integer `x / 0` and `x % 0` return NULL, not an error. Mainline SQLite verified on 2026-04-20 via `/usr/bin/sqlite3 :memory:` for every literal case below. Before 6bv both generators raised `EVAL_DIVISION_BY_ZERO`, producing 42 Rust + 7 C failures in random/aggregates/* where corpus expectations are NULL. No new opcode, no new invariant. The `EVAL_DIVISION_BY_ZERO` error kind is preserved in both cores for ABI symmetry but is unreached by the DIV/MOD paths after this change. IEEE real-division divergence (mainline SQLite returns NULL for `5.0 / 0`; leap engines return IEEE `+inf`/`NaN`) is OUT OF SCOPE for 6bv — tracked separately. Cases below exercise the integer and type-promotion paths only.

cases.name: int-div-zero
cases.description: Baseline: integer `5 / 0` yields NULL (was EVAL_DIVISION_BY_ZERO before 6bv).

cases.name: int-mod-zero
cases.description: Integer modulo-by-zero yields NULL (was EVAL_DIVISION_BY_ZERO before 6bv).

cases.name: neg-div-zero
cases.description: Signed integer LHS: `-5 / 0` yields NULL. Sign of the LHS does not matter.

cases.name: zero-div-zero
cases.description: `0 / 0` yields NULL (integer path — both sides are integer literals).

cases.name: null-div-zero
cases.description: NULL-propagation precedence still holds: NULL / 0 yields NULL by the NULL rule, not by the zero-handling rule. Both rules agree on the result — this case confirms NULL propagation still wins when both apply.

cases.name: null-mod-zero
cases.description: Paired with null-div-zero: NULL %% 0 yields NULL by NULL propagation.

cases.name: div-in-select
cases.description: Row-at-a-time integer DIV: rows with b=0 project NULL, others project the integer quotient. Verified mainline: the b=0 row returns NULL (empty in the CLI output), non-zero rows project 5 and 10 respectively.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);
SELECT a/b FROM t ORDER BY a;

cases.name: mod-in-select
cases.description: Row-at-a-time integer MOD: rows with b=0 project NULL; non-zero b rows return a%b.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);
SELECT a%b FROM t ORDER BY a;

cases.name: agg-with-div-zero
cases.description: SUM over an integer DIV expression where some rows divide by zero. SUM skips NULL per existing aggregate NULL semantics: SUM(10/2, 20/0, 30/3) = SUM(5, NULL, 10) = 15. Verified mainline.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);

cases.name: count-preserved-through-div-zero
cases.description: COUNT counts non-NULL values of its argument (COUNT(expr) skips NULL). Integer-div-by-zero yields NULL, so the zero-divisor row is not counted. Rows (a=10,b=2), (a=20,b=0), (a=30,b=3) -> COUNT(a/b) = 2.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);

cases.name: where-div-zero-skips-row
cases.description: The SQLite-compat quirk interacts with WHERE: `WHERE a/b = 5` with b=0 evaluates the LHS to NULL; comparison NULL = 5 yields NULL; the WHERE gate treats NULL as NOT TRUE and skips the row. Only the row where a/b = 5 (a=10,b=2) is returned.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);
SELECT a FROM t WHERE a/b = 5 ORDER BY a;

cases.name: update-with-div-zero
cases.description: UPDATE with an RHS expression that divides by zero writes NULL (since the expr yields NULL, INTEGER columns accept NULL). Starting row (a=10, b=0): UPDATE t SET a = a/b; leaves a = NULL.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);
